title: An Efficient Local Search Algorithm for Large GD Advertising Inventory Allocation with Multilinear Constraints

problem.claim: GD advertising inventory allocation must accommodate focus ratio requirements involving non-convex multilinear constraints.

gap.claim: Convex-property methods are unsuitable, while mathematical programming and constraint-based heuristic solvers cannot produce high-quality solutions within the time limit.

contributions.claim: A local search framework is proposed for GD advertising inventory allocation with multilinear constraints.
The framework incorporates four new operators for handling multilinear constraints and uses a two-mode algorithmic architecture.
The algorithm is designed to handle general multilinear constraints in GD advertising allocation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their algorithm computes high-quality allocations with better business metrics than state-of-the-art mathematical programming and constraint-based heuristic solvers.
The authors report that the algorithm can handle general multilinear constraints.

narrative_sequence.summary: GD advertising inventory allocation affects publishers' ability to fulfill contract requirements and increase revenue.
Business scenarios may require focus ratios comparing allocated impressions across contracts and media.
Focus ratio requirements create non-convex multilinear constraints that make allocation difficult.
Existing convexity-based methods and available optimization or heuristic solvers are inadequate under the stated time and quality requirements.
The paper proposes a local search framework with new operators and a two-mode architecture, and reports better business metrics than comparator solvers.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework adds specialized operators and a two-mode architecture for multilinear constraints.

interpretation.claim: When constraints are non-convex and standard optimization methods are inadequate, search procedures may need constraint-specific neighborhoods and operating modes.

application.claim: Consider specialized local-search operators and multiple search modes for large allocation problems with similar multilinear requirements.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond GD advertising or under which constraint structures it performs best.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, instance sizes, runtime limits, or numerical business metrics.
The abstract does not describe the four operators, the two modes, or the experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide quantitative comparisons or independent verification.
